contributions.statement: When building internal agent eval tasks from your own repositories' history, strip future commits and the reference fix from the task image (single-commit snapshot, no reachable refs), because leaked future history inflated non-Python SWE-bench-Multilingual scores by up to 8 pp.
contributions.evidence: §6.5 Fig. 5: after cleanup Pass@1 is never higher for 8 models on 300 instances; Opus 4.7 -8.0 pp, Kimi 2.6 -5.0 pp. 2609.08149 later shows similar leakage with weaker (moderate) evidence.

contributions.statement: In a host-neutral agent evaluation runner, export the patch from repository state (git diff after the run) instead of having the model write diff text, which raised one harness from 19.3% to 71.2% resolved with apply failures under 1.5%.
contributions.evidence: §6.1 Table 1: OpenClaw + GLM 5.1 bare vs full adapter. Audit: one harness, one model, and the bare baseline is close to a strawman, so moderate.

contributions.statement: With the model fixed, mature general harnesses landed within about 2 pp of each other while a single weak harness lost up to 24 pp, so evaluate the hosts your engineers use on your own tasks to screen out outliers rather than to rank the top ones.
contributions.evidence: §6.2 Table 2: Hermes 73.1 vs OpenClaw 71.2 (GLM 5.1), 81.7 vs 79.8 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash); GenericAgent 38.5 vs Hermes 62.8 on Qwen 3.6-flash. 3-run means, no SD; Claude Code, Codex and Cursor absent; authors' COI (TokenRhythm) flagged by audit.
relative_to: harness matters with model fixed (SWE-agent ACI)

reason: The contamination finding and the patch-export protocol are concrete practices for any team building its own agent evals; the harness ranking itself adds little because the commercial hosts are missing.
